facts.raw_span: A man in his 80s without a prior history of arrhythmia
cough and shortness of breath during the COVID-19 pandemic
Cardiac auscultation: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops
Pulmonary auscultation: Inspiratory crackles in bilateral bases of the lungs
Regular, narrow complex tachycardia with rate of 170 beats/min

concepts.why: The patient presented with cough and shortness of breath during the COVID-19 pandemic and tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
The patient developed palpitations and the ECG showed regular, narrow complex tachycardia with a rate of 170 beats/min.

aliases: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
concepts.why: The echocardiogram showed mild diastolic dysfunction, which is consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient presented with inspiratory crackles in bilateral bases of the lungs and tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, which is consistent with this diagnosis.

rationales.F02: Cough and shortness of breath are common symptoms of COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome.
rationales.F10: Inspiratory crackles in bilateral bases of the lungs are a common finding in COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome.
rationales.F11: A positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR test is a definitive indicator of COVID-19.
rationales.F12: Regular, narrow complex tachycardia is a characteristic ECG finding of atrial tachycardia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including regular, narrow complex tachycardia with a rate of 170 beats/min and specific P-wave characteristics, strongly support atrial tachycardia, which explains the palpitations.
